headline: Mistakes to Avoid After a Small Fire
articleBody: Dealing with the aftermath of a small fire can be stressful, and it’s easy to make choices that could complicate the cleanup. Knowing what *not* to do is just as important as knowing what to do! One big mistake is delaying cleanup; soot and ash are corrosive and will cause more damage the longer they sit. Another common error is using standard household cleaners on smoke-damaged items. These often contain chemicals that can react with soot, causing permanent stains or setting odors deeper. Don't touch surfaces with your bare hands, as the oils from your skin can combine with soot and make cleanup harder. It’s also a bad idea to try and run your HVAC system or other appliances without a professional inspection; you could spread contaminants or cause further electrical issues. Trying to clean up extensive smoke damage yourself without proper PPE is another no-go – you risk inhaling harmful particles. And finally, forgetting to document everything for your insurance claim is a major oversight. Take photos, keep records, and consult with professionals like First To Respond Restoration early on. We encourage getting multiple estimates, ensuring you make an informed decision for your fire damage restoration needs.
